name: Kacchi Biryani
historicNote: Brought to Dhaka by Mughal and Persian nobility in the 17th-18th centuries, kacchi biryani is defined by dum pukht - raw ("kacchi") marinated meat and parboiled rice are layered together, sealed with a dough rope, and slow-steamed in their own trapped moisture rather than cooked separately and combined, as most other South Asian biryanis are.
whenEaten: The centerpiece dish at Dhaka weddings, Eid gatherings, and other major family celebrations - rarely made as an everyday meal because of the time and mutton it requires.
shortDescription: Mutton and potatoes dum-cooked with fragrant basmati rice, sealed and steamed together in one pot.
headnote: The one non-negotiable step here is the marinade time - at least six hours, ideally overnight - since the yogurt and raw papaya need real time to tenderize the mutton before it ever meets heat. Everything after that (the rice parboiling, the dum seal, the layering) is far more forgiving than it looks.
equipment: Heavy-bottomed handi or dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid
Wheat-flour dough rope for sealing the dum
Tawa or flat griddle to sit under the pot and diffuse heat
miseEnPlace: Soak the basmati rice 30 minutes before cooking, then drain
Deep-fry the sliced onions ahead of time and keep them crisp, uncovered
Marinate the mutton at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, refrigerated

items.name: mutton, bone-in curry-cut
items.prepNote: fat-on pieces, at room temperature before cooking

items.name: whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon stick, green cardamom)
items.prepNote: one full set, added to the parboiling water

items.name: potatoes
items.prepNote: medium, peeled and halved, lightly fried

items.name: fried onion (beresta)
items.prepNote: deep-fried until deep golden, cooled crisp

items.name: ghee
items.prepNote: for drizzling over the top layer

steps.title: Marinate the mutton
steps.instruction: Whisk {0002} until smooth, combine with {0003} and {0004}, stir in {0005} and {0006}, then coat {0001} fully. Cover and refrigerate.
steps.visualCue: Meat edges look slightly pale and opaque, yogurt fully absorbed with no liquid pooling at the bottom
steps.commonMistake: Marinating under 4 hours leaves the meat tough - the yogurt and papaya need real time to break down the connective tissue

steps.title: Parboil the rice
steps.instruction: Boil {0007} with {0008} and {0009} in plenty of water until about 70% done.
steps.technique: 70% parboil - the rice must retain a hard white core
steps.visualCue: A grain bends but snaps, with a hard uncooked centre still visible when bitten
steps.commonMistake: Fully cooking the rice here makes it mushy once it finishes steaming under dum

steps.title: Layer and seal for dum
steps.instruction: Spread the marinated {0001} and {0010} in the base of the handi. Layer the parboiled {0007} on top, then scatter {0011}, drizzle over the bloomed {0012} and {0013}, and finish with {0014}. Seal the lid completely with a rope of dough.
steps.technique: Dum layering - raw marinated meat goes on the bottom so it steams in its own juices under the rice
steps.visualCue: The dough seal is fully closed with no visible gaps or steam escaping
steps.commonMistake: Layering the rice too thickly in one spot traps steam unevenly and leaves some rice undercooked

steps.title: Dum cook (sealed steam)
steps.instruction: Cook over high heat for the first 10 minutes to build internal steam pressure, then place a tawa underneath the pot and drop to the lowest possible flame for the rest of the cooking time.

heat.flameNote: 10 minutes on high to build pressure, then the lowest flame possible with a tawa diffusing heat from below

steps.technique: Dum - the dough-sealed pot traps steam, finishing the rice and cooking the raw meat together without any direct water contact
steps.visualCue: Fragrant steam escapes the moment the seal is broken; the rice is fully fluffy and the mutton is fork-tender
steps.commonMistake: Skipping the tawa under the pot burns the bottom layer of rice before the meat is done

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.instruction: Turn off the heat and leave the sealed pot undisturbed to finish carrying over.
steps.technique: Residual-heat rest, standard for every dum dish
steps.visualCue: Rice grains have fully separated and the surface glistens with rendered ghee
steps.commonMistake: Opening the seal early releases the trapped steam the last of the cooking depends on

chefTips: Fry the onions a full day ahead - they crisp better once completely cooled and stay crunchy longer under the rice
If the dum smells like it is catching at the bottom before 30 minutes are up, the flame is too high - lower it further rather than opening the seal to check
donenessSummary: Rice grains are separate and fluffy with no raw core; mutton pulls apart with light fork pressure; a thin layer of ghee has visibly separated at the surface.
platingNote: Bring the sealed handi to the table and break the dough seal in front of guests - the aroma release on opening is part of the dish.
storageNote: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat covered with a splash of water on low heat to restore moisture.

substitutions.impact: Cuts total time by roughly 40% and gives a milder flavor

regionalVariations: Old Dhaka households use more ghee and a deeper-brown fried onion, and some add a few extra drops of kewra water at the final dum stage
